...of the eternal God, declared to all the nations for the obedience of faith.” And from this the light that was to be revealed to the nations shone forth upon those who had been placed in darkness and the shadow of death — the light of which God speaks through the prophet: “I have appointed you to be a light to the nations, that you may be for salvation to the ends of the earth.” For when Christ commanded his apostles to go forth into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature, they went out and preached everywhere, allowing no place to remain hidden from the heavenly teaching: “μὴ νήσους, μὴ ἤπειρον, μηδʼ εἴτινα τρίτην ἀνθρώποις κατοικίαν ἡ φύσις ἐδίδου — neither the islands, nor the mainland, nor any third dwelling-place that nature had granted to humankind,” as Gregory of Nyssa puts it. And so was fulfilled what God had long before foretold through Isaiah: “I will send from among them to the nations in the ocean, and to the most remote islands, which had not heard my fame nor seen my glory, that they may declare my glory among the nations.” For “the word of God” — these are Augustine’s words — “has been preached not on the mainland alone, but also on the islands set in the midst of the sea; and these too are full of Christians, full of the servants of God. For the sea does not separate them from him who made the sea.

Where ships can reach, can the words of God not reach?”

And indeed Britain received the gospel from its very first rising. To this island — numb with icy cold and lying, as it were, in a remoter recess of the earth, far from the visible sun — that true Sun, shining not from the temporal firmament alone but from the highest citadel of the heavens that transcends all time, displaying to the whole world the dazzling flash of his glory, first granted his rays, that is, his precepts; and that Sun is Christ. This he did, as we know, in the closing years of Tiberius Caesar, in whose reign his religion was spread without any hindrance — for though the senate was unwilling, the emperor had threatened death to those who informed against the soldiers of that same faith.
